phaseNote: hud 7.0 and perf 6.0. The item slot and minimap are fixed and the frame cost is down a quarter with the simulation untouched. Both still fail on something measured: a winning position plate cut in half by the letterbox, and a frame-time instrument that cannot see the frames it exists for.

pieces.name: Effects & spectacle
pieces.verdict: 6.5/10 after three rounds. Sparks, tyre smoke, boost flames, marks and impacts all firing off the right events.
pieces.gap: Every smoke puff is a flat-alpha polygon with a hard cookie-cutter rim — at 9x zoom you can count a 16-gon silhouette — so the one particle on screen in every frame reads as a cutout disc rather than smoke.

pieces.name: Items
pieces.verdict: 7/10 after three rounds. Boxes, roulette, full item set, coins, and a genuinely strong hit vocabulary — banana spins you 1.00 rotation in 0.73s and drops you 53 to 23 m/s; a green shell flips you 1.08 rotations in 1.02s and launches you.
pieces.gap: The blooper blacks out ~66% of the central play area at up to 0.97 opacity for six seconds. Mario Kart ink is a nuisance you race through; this one is a blindfold.

pieces.name: CPU racers
pieces.verdict: Rubber-band cut. Finishing spread over 3 laps of Cone Canyon is now 1st 2:18.893, 8th +1:34.852 — was the entire field inside 0.811s.
pieces.gap: Overcorrected into three clumps rather than a spread: 2nd/3rd/4th land within 0.16s of each other, 5th/6th/7th within 0.16s, and 8th is over a lap adrift.

pieces.name: HUD & minimap
pieces.verdict: 7.0/10 after two rounds. The item slot is no longer a void — it has a designed idle and draws its item — the roulette runs its whole spin, and the minimap gives each rival a readable marker instead of seven identical dots.
pieces.gap: At the finish, the one frame the whole race builds to, the position plate this module keeps on screen because it is the answer comes to rest with its bottom 40% and its entire ordinal suffix behind the letterbox bar. The player who wins is shown a sawn-off gold 1 with no ST.

pieces.name: World dressing
pieces.verdict: 6.5/10 after two rounds. Crowds, floodlights, marshal posts, flags, grandstands, cranes and roadworks dressing, all instanced.
pieces.gap: On the straights the 0-60m band on both sides is bare barrier and empty dirt, and nothing within 100m of the camera moves. Park the kart and advance 1.4s: the only pixels that change are sky clouds and the exhaust.

pieces.name: Music & sound
pieces.verdict: 6.5/10 after two rounds. A full synthesized stack: per-vehicle engines, drift, impacts, items, music, positional audio. No audio files.
pieces.gap: A two-second drift has no tyre scrub at all — 0.09 dB difference across the module own documented 1900 Hz band between slip 0 and slip 1. The corner the player lives in is silent apart from one 80ms tick.

pieces.name: Race flow & results
pieces.verdict: 7.5/10 after two rounds, the highest this project has recorded. Grid, lights, flag, wrap and results state machine; the rocket-start window measured and corrected to a single beat ending on the green.
pieces.gap: Nothing in the game ever celebrates. The finish camera executes a real 2.4s, 60-degree victory orbit onto a machine doing exactly what it did on lap one, and the results sheet then paints the world out at 97% opacity so you never see it anyway.

pieces.name: Front-end & menus
pieces.verdict: 7.0/10 after two rounds. Title, class, roster and circuit screens, all drawn geometry, with shadows, spring selection and a working course card.
pieces.gap: The screen where you pick your machine is monochrome. All eight roster cells render as the same dark grey chip with a white pictogram, because the machine colour is a radial wash anchored below the cell and unselected cells are knocked to saturate(.55) on top of that.

pieces.name: Course roster
pieces.verdict: Held back deliberately: the roster could not look like four places until the renderer consumed what a course declares. That wiring now exists.

pieces.name: Theme wiring
pieces.verdict: 6.5/10 after two rounds, blind pick Mario Kart. Four real ground surfaces with their own colour ramps and procedural detail maps, a theme resolver that throws by name on an unknown key, and prop sets placed in the band the chase camera looks at.
pieces.gap: Not one piece of static world geometry casts a shadow. Barriers, masts, pines, grandstands, containers, silos and boulders all meet the ground at a hard edge, so every course reads as a well-painted backdrop with stickers standing on it.

pieces.name: Performance
pieces.verdict: 6.0/10 after two rounds. Real cuts landed: 509,822 triangles across 299 draw calls, down from 678,804 across 370, with the simulation bit-identical — same seed, same 47.825 m/s, same 512.926m.
pieces.gap: The instrument is still broken one layer down. Round 1 failed the governor for a warm-up gate that could not fire on a slow machine; the gate is now counted in seconds, and the seconds accumulator has the same property — STALL_MS discards the exact frames the governor exists to measure, so liveSeconds accrued 1.66s across 200s of wall time and it read priming, samples 0, for three minutes.

pieces.name: Whole-game coherence
pieces.verdict: 7.0 then 6.5 across two rounds. The score fell because the critic got deeper, not because the game got worse: round 2 measured things round 1 never reached. Field spread fixed from 0.811s to 24-94s, the AI drifts, the review sheet stopped lying, and the four on-screen instruction languages collapsed onto one rail.
pieces.gap: The race is composed like a spectator replay rather than something you are driving. The chase rig sat high and far with the kart at 4-8% of frame height, so every asset the game is proudest of played too small to land. Camera now fixed; the item slot is still an empty black square dead centre of the frame, and the results sheet covers the podium it just lit.

log.text: Wave 6 landed. 509,822 triangles across 299 draw calls, down from 678,804 across 370, with the simulation bit-identical. The item slot is no longer a black hole.
Coherence pass complete. The field now finishes 24-94s apart instead of inside 0.811s, the AI charges mini-turbos, and the review sheet no longer captions frames that do not show what they claim.
Coherence round 1 scored 7.0/10 and named the real gap: the front-end is first-party and the race it launches into has no stakes. Round 2 is aimed at the racing, not the chrome.
Player feedback beat the critics: steering was mirrored and nothing said what the buttons were. Both fixed, verified and deployed. Coherence survey found 14 seams and the smoothing pass is underway.
Wave 5 landed. Smoke passes at 62.6 m/s and 747k triangles. The review sheet confirms the critics: nothing in the frame casts a shadow, so the coherence pass goes next rather than more piece work.
All three wave-4 pieces failed round 1 with measured gaps. Courses turned out to be blocked by the renderer ignoring what a course declares, so a theme-wiring piece was added ahead of it.
Wave 4 building: race flow & results, front-end menus, three more courses. Added the perf brief and the coherence pass to the roster.

AI 5.5, audio 6.5, world 6.5 — all fail, all merged. The AI critic ran two full 120s races at 10Hz and found the field spends 17.5% of the race in the gravel, falling off at the same two named corners every lap. The audio critic measured a 0.09 dB difference in the drift-scrub band between no slip and full slip, against a 6 dB pass bar. The world critic parked the kart and advanced 1.4 seconds of visual time: nothing in the bottom 60% of frame changed.
AI, audio and world dressing dispatched. Items, effects and HUD carry their directives to a later polish wave — they are at 6.5-7 and improving, while these three do not exist at all.

Six critics, three rounds, still no pass — and the reviews are getting better. The blooper critique came with a numeric pass condition: re-run the same crop and require fraction-below-luminance-60 under 0.40. The particle critique came with an acceptance test: re-shoot the train funnel at 9x zoom, no straight edge traceable. This is what a review loop looks like when it stops guessing.

All three pieces failed and go back. Items 7/10, HUD 6.5/10, effects 5.5/10 — every blind A/B went to Mario Kart. The critics measured rather than eyeballed: CSS opacity sampled every four fixed steps across 40s, particle-atlas alpha peaks read off the live texture, spark streak length computed in metres against the length of the kart.

Wave 2 was dead for 11.5 hours before anyone noticed. The container suspended overnight and silently killed both in-flight agents and the check-in job. Liveness is now proven by transcript timestamp every 12 minutes, because files and processes both outlive the agents that made them.

Items, effects and HUD dispatched. The item system does not exist yet, and without it this is a time trial rather than a kart racer. Effects are equally absent — a drift currently looks identical to driving straight.
Wave 1 merged to main. Engine, review harness, physics, camera, track, art direction and the seven-machine cast. Verified: typecheck clean, smoke passes at 8 racers and 51.8 m/s.

Wave 1 stalled at 13 of 15 agents. Its work is merged and verified, but two pieces never returned a closing verdict, so no wave 1 piece is marked passed. They go back through a critic rather than being credited on trust.

Karts were vanishing from their own chase camera. The engine derived the frame-blend factor from an accumulator the harness bypasses, producing an alpha of -438 — every interpolation became an extrapolation and drew each kart two hundred metres behind itself. Clamped where the number is handed out.

Five foundation pieces dispatched. Kart feel, camera, track, art direction and the cast each go to an owner agent, then to a critic that plays the real game and compares it blind against Mario Kart 8. Pieces loop until the critic can no longer name a gap.

Capture harness made practical. Shots now fast-forward the simulation without drawing and render only the settling moment. The nine-shot review sheet went from timing out at 290s to 99s — which is what makes repeated review affordable.

Four defects found by looking, not reading. The road mesh was wound backwards and was being discarded entirely by backface culling — karts appeared to float over bare ground. The camera inherited stale state between races, and un-rendered landing impulses accumulated until the camera launched 350m into the air.

Engine, contracts and harness in place. Deterministic 120Hz simulation with interpolated rendering, a TypeScript contract every module compiles against, and window.__GAME so reviewers can drive and photograph the real game rather than trust a description of it.
